senses.gloss: (transl. of cursor) mail-carrier, despatch-bearer. Tanḥ. Ekeb 11 ד׳ שהיה מהלך וכ׳ a cursor who travelled with an ordinance in his hand.
units: <cite ref="Shabbat 19a:7">Sabb. 19ᵃ</cite> <he>קביע ד׳ במתא</he> Ms. M. (ed. <cite ref="D01080"><he>בי ד׳</he></cite>) the mail-carrier (ed. the post office) is permanently located in town.

senses.gloss: (Pers. dâvar, judge, ruler, Fl.) בֵּי ד׳ the (Persian) circuit court consisting of regular law scholars, opp. דייני דמגיסתא squires in country places ignorant of the law.
units: <cite ref="Bava Kamma 114a:1">B. Kam. 114ᵃ</cite> (Ms. R. <he>אַבֵּי ד׳</he> in the &c., Ms. M. <he>בודאור</he>, corr. acc.).
<cite ref="Gittin 58b:9">Gitt. 58ᵇ</cite> <he>כיון דאיכא בי ד׳ וכ׳</he> since there exists (in Persia) a lawful court, and he did not sue (the tax officer).
Ab. Zar. 26ᵃ נקיטא לי זימנא לבי ד׳ I am summoned to court (and have no time). [In later Hebr. literature בי דואר is used in the sense of post-office.]
